\section{Conditional transport and effective Hessian}\label{app:marginal}

We justify the two analytic tools used in Theorem~\ref{thm:main} with the
hard fiber ball $\cD_r$.  Let $D\subset\R^n$ be compact, convex, and have
nonempty interior.  Suppose $V_y\in C^2$ on a neighborhood of
$Y\times D$ and $D_z^2V_y\succeq\alpha\Id$.

\begin{lemma}[Differentiation and Hessian identity]\label{lem:hessian-identity}
For $Z(y)=\int_De^{-V_y(z)}\dd z$ and $F=-\log Z$,
\[
 DF=\E_y[D_yV_y],\qquad
 D^2F=\E_y[D_y^2V_y]-\Cov_y(D_yV_y,D_yV_y).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
On the compact product, the integrand and its first two $y$ derivatives are
uniformly bounded.  Dominated differentiation gives the first formula.
Differentiating the normalized expectation gives the covariance correction
and hence the second formula.  The boundary does not depend on $y$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Covariance bound on a convex body]\label{lem:bl-body}
If $D_z^2V_y\succeq\alpha\Id$, then for every smooth scalar $f$,
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_{\nu_y}(f)
 \le\E_{\nu_y}\!\left[\ip{\nabla f}{(D_z^2V_y)^{-1}\nabla f}\right]
 \le\alpha^{-1}\E_{\nu_y}\norm{\nabla f}^2.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Approximate the indicator of $D$ by $e^{-b_m}$, where $b_m$ is a smooth convex
barrier increasing to $+\infty$ off $D$.  The usual Brascamp--Lieb inequality
\cite{BrascampLieb1976} applies to $V_y+b_m$ and its inverse Hessian is bounded
above by $(D_z^2V_y)^{-1}$.  Monotone localization and dominated convergence
give the claim.
\end{proof}

Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:bl-body} to
$f=v\cdot D_yS_t$ for a unit retained vector $v$.  The mixed derivative bound
is $\norm{D_zD_yS_t}\le(1/80)/t$, while
$D_z^2S_t\succeq(3/80)/t$.  Consequently
\[
 t\operatorname{Var}(v\cdot D_yS_t)
 \le\frac{(1/80)^2}{3/80}.
\]
Together with Lemma~\ref{lem:hessian-identity}, this gives
\eqref{eq:effective-hessian-bound}.

For transport, the Bakry--\'{E}mery argument with the same convex barriers
gives a logarithmic Sobolev constant $1/\alpha$.  If
$\norm{\nabla_zV_y-\nabla_zV_{y'}}\le L\norm{y-y'}$, the logarithmic Sobolev
inequality bounds the relative entropy by
$L^2\norm{y-y'}^2/(2\alpha)$.  Its quadratic transport consequence
\cite{OttoVillani2000} yields
\[
 W_2(\nu_y,\nu_{y'})\le\frac L\alpha\norm{y-y'}.
\]
Here $L=(1/80)/t$ and $\alpha=(3/80)/t$, giving $1/3$.
